subject: Evaluation: cost equivalence scorecard and departure play
messages:
From: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@cloudforge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: CloudForge Sales <sales@cloudforge.com>
Date: 2025-08-10T14:13:00Z
Subject: CloudForge Q3 rates + potential match for Redwood

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. I promised to share our Q3 rate sheet and a quick note on where we can be flexible. Attached is CloudForge_RateSheet_Q3.pdf with standard discounts. We reviewed the numbers you shared about your current run rate with your incumbent and believe we can match the list rate on token pricing if Redwood can commit to a 12-month minimum and allow us a 30-day migration window for the initial usage ramp.

Two quick clarifications we need from your side to firm this up:
- Your token mix (generative vs. embeddings) and 95th percentile token length distribution.
- Whether you require dedicated instances or are fine with shared capacity for the pilot.

If you can send a short profile (1 page) I can put together an equivalence proposal (pricing + migration credit) by mid-week.

Best,
Peter Lowe
Account Exec | CloudForge
Attachments: CloudForge_RateSheet_Q3.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@cloudforge.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-11T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: CloudForge Q3 rates + potential match for Redwood

Hi Peter,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the rate sheet. Connor (cc'd) is pulling the usage slices — we'll send a 1-page profile today that shows token mix, seq length percentiles, and peak concurrency.

A few context items up front so your commercial team can align the equivalence:
- We are evaluating a full replacement for a subset of customers (pilot ~3M tokens/mo) and a staggered rollout to larger cohorts.
- Important to us: equivalent latency SLO for chat workloads (p50/p95), and KV-cache behavior for chat sessions.
- Migration credit preference: we like a two-stage credit (pilot credit + go-live uplift) rather than an up-front one-off.

Can you include in the equivalence proposal: a side-by-side of packaging (hosted vs dedicated options), egress and storage assumptions, and a proposed migration-credit schedule? That'll help us score the offer against incumbent costs.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Manager, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@cloudforge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: CloudForge Sales <sales@cloudforge.com>
Date: 2025-08-11T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: CloudForge Q3 rates + potential match for Redwood

Mina — thanks, got the profile and Connor's notes. Attached is CF_equivalence_proposal.xlsx which includes: a blended token rate to match your incumbent's effective per-token, a 2-part migration credit (pilot: 30% credit for first 60 days, go-live: one-time credit equal to 10% of first 3 months' committed spend), and optional dedicated pools at a +12% premium.

Key asks from our ops side before we finalize:
1) Confirmation on expected peak qps and typical sequence length at p95 so we can validate gen-latency guarantees.
2) A short runbook around how you handle model fallbacks / graceful degradation — we need to mirror behavior for parity.

If agreed, we can produce a term sheet and a statement of work for migration services.

Regards,
Peter Lowe
Account Exec | CloudForge
Attachments: CF_equivalence_proposal.xlsx
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@cloudforge.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-12T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: CloudForge Q3 rates + potential match for Redwood

Peter — appreciate the proposal, and nice detail. A couple of internal notes that will affect how we score equivalence (and therefore the economics we can accept):

- Technical parity: matching per-token economics is necessary but not sufficient. We need documented p50/p95 latency on 8k/16k contexts with the same concurrency profiles. Also confirm whether your dedicated pool offers GPU pinning and the exact instance SKUs.

- Operational risk: we need a 90-day rollback plan and an SLA credit structure tied to p95 latency degradations. Our legal team will care about warranty and indemnity carveouts for model drift / hallucination impact.

- Packaging/commit structure: We favor a phased committed spend ramp (3 months pilot at 50% commit, then go-live 100%) with migration credits paid against committed spend. This helps our finance team model ARR impact.

Attached is a short comparison checklist and a blank comparison_table_v1.xlsx to capture the data points we need on latency, KV cache behavior, model versions supported, and maintenance windows. If CloudForge can provide p95 numbers and confirm dedicated SKU details by end of day Thursday, we can move to a term sheet review on Friday.

On process: please route the final term sheet and proposed SOW via DocuSign to legal@redwoodinference.com and include your HubSpot deal id in the subject.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Strategy | Redwood Inference
Attachments: comparison_table_v1.xlsx
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@cloudforge.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-12T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: CloudForge Q3 rates + potential match for Redwood

Thanks all — quick summary and next steps from our side so nothing falls through the cracks: 

1) CloudForge to provide: p50/p95 latency tables for 8k and 16k contexts (matched concurrency), dedicated pool SKU list with GPU SKU naming, and a redlineable term sheet that includes the two-stage migration credit. (Peter)
2) Redwood will: populate comparison_table_v1.xlsx with our measured p50/p95 and KV-cache behavior and send redwood-econ-scorecard.xlsx (attached) that scores CF's proposal against incumbent economics. (Mina / Connor)
3) Timeline: If CloudForge provides the technical datapack and term sheet by EOD Thursday (2025-08-14T23:59:00Z), Naomi's team will do a term-sheet review and circulate legal redlines by Monday.

Attachments: redwood-econ-scorecard.xlsx — this contains an economic equivalence model (pilot vs committed) and recommended packaging preferences. Please confirm receipt and whether DocuSign will be used for the final term sheet.

Mina Haddad
Sr. Manager, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference
